transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me a bit about what brings you in to see me today?

I've been feeling really overwhelmed lately because I keep hearing voices that other people can't hear. On top of that, for the past few weeks, I've had this extreme energy where I can't stop talking and my mood is just swinging all over the place. It's gotten really hard to manage, so I wanted to get some help.
Do you experience these voices only during times when your mood is very high or low, or do you also hear them when your mood is relatively stable?

I definitely hear them even when my mood is relatively stable. There have been periods, sometimes for two weeks or more, where my mood felt completely normal but the voices were still there just as clear as ever.

latest_inference.note: Previously, the candidates were Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type) and Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features. The patient reported experiencing auditory hallucinations during periods of mood stability (lasting two weeks or more). According to DSM-5-TR criteria, for a diagnosis of Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features, psychotic symptoms must occur exclusively during a mood episode. Since the patient reports psychotic symptoms independent of mood episodes, Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type) is now the most accurate diagnosis.
